key_insight: BAR helps an LLM make post-discharge risk predictions by exploring medical knowledge graphs in a budget-aware way and requiring evidence to be verifiable and citable.
clinical_relevance: This could make EHR-based risk predictions more explainable for retrospective review by linking outputs to traceable medical knowledge rather than hidden model reasoning.
method: Builds disease-specific evidence graphs from medical KGs with support scores and provenance.
Uses a plan-navigate-verify LLM loop to retrieve evidence within a patient-specific budget and revise when verification fails.
Trains the reasoning policy with rewards for predictive gain, lower acquisition cost, and citation integrity.
evidence_signal: Across 8 diseases and 3 prediction horizons on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV, BAR improved AUPRC by 3.4 points over the strongest baseline, raised citation precision from 59.8% to 77.9%, and used 62-65% of the budget cap.
watch_item: Performance and citation quality depend on KG coverage, provenance quality, and careful budget tuning, so real-world deployment may need validation on local data.
paper_title: Cite What You Explore: Budget-Aware LLM Reasoning over Medical KGs with Verifiable Evidence
